page: Amazon Web Services i7i.large is an entry-tier storage-optimized virtual machine driven by the AWS Nitro System. It operates on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with one physical core providing two dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 320 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides 16 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is a 468 GB NVMe SSD local storage volume, alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and zero onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight significant single-threaded processing capabilities alongside the throughput constraints inherent to a two-vCPU footprint. The instance scored 2290.0 on Geekbench single-core testing, positioning it in the top ten percent of tested servers. It demonstrates strong single-threaded throughput in data compression tests, reaching 34.55 GB/s in gzip compression and 13.93 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, multi-threaded results, such as the Geekbench multi-core score of 2797.0 and stress-ng multi-core execution, reflect the bottleneck of a single physical core. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 21.97 GB/s, while Redis SET operations sustain 3.05 million operations per second.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the instance functions as a low-overhead entry point for applications requiring fast local storage and ample memory allocation per thread without the expense of higher vCPU tiers. The primary architectural tradeoff is its modest multi-core capacity and 1 Gbps network limit. The i7i.large is well-fitted for low-to-medium throughput transactional databases, local caching, search index nodes, and log ingestion pipelines requiring fast NVMe scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.large is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8559C processor with two dedicated vCPUs across one physical core. It is configured with 16 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a 468 GB NVMe SSD local storage drive with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Driven by fifth-generation Intel Xeon architecture, it demonstrates top-tier single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 2290.0 and robust single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core throughput remains restricted by the two-thread limit. The instance delivers a balanced, cost-effective resource profile for storage-heavy workloads such as standalone transactional databases, Redis caching layers, log aggregation, and local staging tasks that rely on high-speed NVMe storage rather than extensive parallel compute.
